children: The two-day conference of chief ministers and state finance ministers organised by the Finance Ministry concluded on Saturday, following extensive deliberations on policy priorities for India's development journey towards Viksit Bharat and pathways for sustained, inclusive and broad-based growth.

The two-day conference was attended by the Union Minister for Finance and chief ministers of Assam, Delhi, Goa, Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir, Keralam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Nagaland; Deputy Chief Ministers of Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, and Odisha were in attendance.

Besides, Finance Ministers of Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Tripura, UP, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal, as well as senior officers of states and the Finance Ministry, were also present.

The conference witnessed a series of deliberations across two days on India's financing requirements and pathways for sustained, inclusive and broad-based growth, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.

On the first day, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) Secretary Anuradha Thakur set out the context in the inaugural session, highlighting that the journey towards Viksit Bharat rests on deep complementarities and multi-tiered partnership between the Union and states.

She mentioned that macroeconomic stability and fiscal prudence have received global recognition, including four sovereign rating upgrades by major international rating agencies over the past 16-17 months, with JCR recently upgrading India by one notch from BBB+ to A-.

Thakur emphasised that the scale of transformation to attain Viksit Bharat could not be met by Government Budgets alone. Private-sector financing, innovative financing mechanisms and stronger cooperation across levels of government will play a critical role.

During the day, the keynote address was delivered by N K Singh, former Chairman of the 15th Finance Commission, it said, adding that former Maharashtra Additional Chief Secretary and Finance Secretary Sudhir Shrivastava presented the state's perspective on financing Viksit Bharat.

The second day commenced with a session on "Financing Agriculture Sector Transformation," moderated by Devesh Chaturvedi, former Secretary, Department of Agriculture. The keynote address was delivered by Harsh Kumar Bhanwala, Public Interest Director and Chairman of MCX and former Nabard chairman.
In his remarks during the concluding session, Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said Viksit Bharat depends on Viksit Rajya.

He outlined three priorities for States: creating an enabling environment for private investment through the availability of land, power and logistics, supported by effective single-window clearances; improving the quality of investment through robust project-preparation pipelines and credible project reports to facilitate access to domestic and multilateral finance, alongside directing credit towards underserved districts with growth potential; and strengthening States' own capital expenditure despite fiscal constraints.
He also underlined the need for raising capital outlay from approximately 2.4 per cent to 3 per cent of GSDP by 2031-32.

Nageswaran concluded by underscoring the dual imperative before India: sustaining the long-term development journey towards 2047 while accelerating resource mobilisation over the next five years, when global financing opportunities remain available.
State Bank of India Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty addressed the topic of 'Sources of Finance from Banking Sector ' in the concluding session of the two-day conference.

After attending the Conference on Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat, Brijendra Prasad Yadav, Minister for Commercial Taxes and Finance, Bihar, said the Prime Minister’s vision of a developed India by 2047 encompasses the development of the power sector, agriculture and infrastructure.
Rajesh Dharmani, Minister of Technical Education, Vocational & Industrial Training, Himachal Pradesh, said, Viksit Bharat will be called Viksit Bharat only when there are Viksit states.

There is a big step towards this, and it is really appreciable. But where there is talk of agriculture and technology, energy transition, there are some issues which are state-specific and need to be addressed, he said.

"All states appreciated the initiative taken by the Union Finance Minister to bring all the states onto one platform about financing the needs of Viksit Bharat. All states participated very well. Chief Ministers of certain states, Finance Ministers of certain states, and all government officials participated," Gujarat Finance Minister Kanubhai Desai said.
Speaking after the conference, West Bengal Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta said the two-day conference on financing Viksit Bharat was very instructive.

title: FinMin's two-day conference with CMs, state FMs concludes; deliberates on Viksit Bharat roadmap
